cells.tense: Right now the questions are still live in you, and you are asking them on purpose.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been treating as settled and ask somebody one real question about it — then stop talking and hear the whole answer.
cells.core:
Here, now, you can hold an open question without needing the answer in the same breath. You ask because you want to know, not to steer the conversation, and that's why people tell you things they didn't plan to. Enough light comes to take the next step and you take it, and the uncertainty further out doesn't spook you the way it spooks the people beside you.

That's the skill in this stretch, though — the asking is what you bring and the direction is what keeps arriving. If the questions stop and you start supplying answers out of what you already think, the stretch goes flat and you're just another person guessing. So hand it one more question before you leave it alone today.

Ask it out loud and wait through the silence after it.

cells.tense: You are racing toward an answer before the question has even settled into shape.
cells.ask: Leave one question open on purpose today — write it down unanswered and go do something else for an hour.
cells.core:
Ahead of you there's a version where this is all figured out, and you're already living there. So every open question gets rushed to a conclusion, every ambiguity gets a theory built over it, and you call that being on top of it. You're not moving through the fog — you're shouting coordinates into it and calling whatever answers back a road. By the time the real asking arrives, with an actual person in it, you've already asked it ten times in your head.

Under the hurry there's something you do well: you know what you think, and it usually holds. That's what the haste is trying to protect, and it doesn't need protecting. Let one thing stay undecided and find out what that's like.

Just stop deciding for an hour and let today supply the missing piece.

cells.tense: You stopped asking a long time ago, and the not-asking has outlasted whatever started it.
cells.ask: Describe out loud one thing you can't figure out right now — to anyone — without trying to solve it while you speak.
cells.core:
The curiosity is still in you and the asking isn't. You'll say you're not a big talker, or that you're waiting for the right moment, but the moment keeps being now and the question keeps not coming. You stand at the edge of conversations and watch them go, and the open stuff stays inside where nobody can meet it. What you understand hasn't left you. You just stopped handing it over.

Nothing here needs diagnosing. Start smaller than that. Say one unfinished thing to one person and let it sit unfinished in the air between you. That's the whole move, and it's worth doing before you're sure it will work.

Say it badly, and let that be fine.

cells.tense: You are already steering the conversation into the open, and you still call it just following along.
cells.ask: Catch one moment today where you asked a question and changed the room, and say plainly that you did it.
cells.core:
You're the one picking the direction more often than you'd admit — asking the question that opens a thing up, letting a silence run so someone else fills it, waiting a beat rather than pushing. It works. It's working right now in the rooms you're in. But you describe it as just being curious, just going with it, just seeing what happens, and the steering goes uncounted. Your own hand on the wheel is the one thing you won't look at.

The skill is real whether or not you name it. That's what leaving it unnamed costs: it looks like luck and it isn't, so it can't be leaned on or improved. It just keeps arriving like something that happens to you.

Own one moment where you chose the question on purpose.
